gaps.note: Cut from Daniel to wide shot, F1 starts speaking mid-sentence.
Cut to Mark laughing, Kevin starts talking.
Cut from Daniel to wide shot.

stage_a.note: Sustained smiling and energetic delivery throughout the pitch.
High energy and engaged tone when delivering the ask and mission.
Friendly greeting and approachable demeanor, though mostly focused on script.

venture.description: A portable beverage cooler with built-in freezing gel that eliminates the need for ice.
venture.note: The founders ask for $150,000 for 15% equity.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Introduces himself, the company Chill Systems, and the Chiller product.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Brian enters carrying a bag of ice, apologizing for being late.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Chase says the Chiller doesn't need ice.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Brian complains about stopping for ice and breaks the bag on the floor.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Chase explains he froze the Chiller and loaded drinks which are now cold.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Brian notes the drinks will be cold for a while.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Chase shows it chills many types of cans and bottles, including champagne.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Brian agrees it can hold all that.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Chase calls it the future of portable cooling, saving time, money, and the environment.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Brian drops a messy cooler of melting ice to show the problem.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Chase highlights the sustainable solution, reducing water waste and single-use plastics.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Brian states the ask of $150,000 for 15 percent equity.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Chase invites the sharks to try their samples with chilled drinks.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori points out the cooler can hold either cans or a bottle.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Chase confirms Lori's observation.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Robert remarks that the product is incredibly versatile.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin notes it only holds three cans and he would drink them quickly.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Chase explains it cools three beers at a time, allowing users to swap warm ones in.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori asks how long the Chiller stays cold.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Chase replies that it stays cold for six hours.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Robert asks what their sales have been.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Brian states they have done $111,000 in sales to date, including Kickstarter.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark asks what the cost of the product is.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Brian admits the cost of the unit in front of them is awful.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Chase starts to say something but is cut off.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Brian explains the unit cost $18 to build and they imported 350 units.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark asks if the cost is now $22.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Brian says they added sleeves which cost another $11.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark asks if the cost is up to $32.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Brian confirms it went all the way up to $37 for that unit.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin clarifies if that is the cost to make it.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Brian explains that was the first run, and they have since brought the cost down to $18.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark asks if they are selling into retail at a loss.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Brian confirms they sell into retail at a loss at $30 to prove the market.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Chase states it is the first sustainable portable beverage chiller.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daniel questions the claim that it is the only sustainable cooler.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Robert points out the large amount of plastic in the product despite saving plastic bags.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Chase explains it is built to last forever and the materials are recyclable.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Robert counters that the plastic bag is also recyclable.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Chase argues that only 9% of thrown away plastic is actually recycled.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daniel asks why they chose to enter the crowded cooler space.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Brian shares they worked at Google and Apple and built this on the side for two years.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori asks if they are still working at their jobs.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Brian says they quit two years ago to do this full time.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori asks if they are making money to sustain themselves.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Brian answers they have not taken a salary since leaving their jobs.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin jokingly offers to make a call to get their jobs back.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Chase politely declines, saying they are happy and believe in the mission.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin dramatizes how they left promising careers to be pulled in by a cooler.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Chase agrees with Kevin's dramatic summary.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin reiterates that they are now here with a cooler.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori asks who their number one competitor is.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Brian answers that their main competitor is ice.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori repeats their answer with a smile.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin talks about his anger management, then questions the valuation for a cooler.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Brian insists they are not out of their minds.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin asks why they would make a chotchkie cooler when there are a million out there.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Chase defends the product as sustainable and convenient.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin says he hates the plastic and the sustainability claim, and declares he is out.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark criticizes their presentation for not sticking to features, and exits.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daniel says the social mission shouldn't be a crutch, and the product must stand on its own.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Chase argues the mission is not a crutch but their reason for commitment.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Brian adds they wanted to make a difference rather than just becoming millionaires.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Robert says Brian's reasoning doesn't make any sense.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Brian explains they also wanted to learn because they weren't learning enough at their jobs.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Robert says their story has lapses of credibility and calls it a bad presentation, then exits.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori says they need to get the cost down for people to buy in, and exits.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daniel expresses doubt about the business size but encourages them to pursue their dreams, and exits.

decisions.note: Hates the product, thinks it's a chotchkie, doesn't buy the sustainability claim.
Bad presentation, didn't stick to features.
Lapses of credibility in the story, bad presentation.
Cost is too high, needs to be more affordable.
Not confident it's a huge business.

record.notes: F1 and F2 pitch together. The sharks are highly critical of the presentation and the product's sustainability claims.
